contract: A wide bus export is ONE quantity for every bus it carries, named on the file's title line: "Bus Hourly 'LMP ($/MWh)' Data for Year 2035". So the rule is a property of the FILE, not of a column, and it is resolved from the unit in that title. Two rules are resolved from that unit. `temporal` says how HOURS combine. `class` says how BUSES combine: EXTENSIVE and RATE sum across a bus axis, INTENSIVE does not -- a bus export carries one quantity per file, so an intensive quantity's weight is in another table and `spatialOf` in src/tables/bus/rules.ts refuses rather than weighting across slots. There is still no `series` key and no `weight` key: the spatial rule is `class`, not a second field to keep in step with it. SUM means a period total over the filtered hours is meaningful; MEAN means it is not, and the stats table shows no total at all rather than a plausible wrong one. Resolution: exact match on `unit` (case-sensitive), else no rule -- an unrecognised unit gets MEAN and no total, never a guess. `quantities` is a RECORD of the columns this exporter has been seen to emit, and nothing in src/ reads it. Its job is to fail a test: tests/test_kernels_bus.mjs asserts every entry resolves to a unit this file carries a rule for, so a newly-observed column whose unit is unknown is caught when it is written down rather than discovered as a quantity missing from a groups dropdown. Add a column here when you meet one; if the test then fails, add its unit above rather than deleting the entry.

units.note: An LMP is a price: the sum of hourly prices is not a price. The figure over the kept hours is the unweighted mean of those hours. Combining BUSES is refused for the same reason -- the load that would weight it is in another table.
MW is a rate. Summed over a filtered set of hours it is neither MW nor MWh, so no total is offered.
